description.message: Shows how often each train on your bahn.de results ran 20+ minutes late, and which one could free your saver ticket.

openSearch.message: Open a bahn.de search to see odds here.

privacy.message: Loads train files from the Kurt site (or your own server), which sees your IP address and which trains you look at. Transitous gets start, destination, date, time, your IP address and an extension identifier that is the same for everyone. Chrome stores settings; Google syncs them if sync is on.

unreachable.message: Unreachable: no odds until the server is back

originRequired.message: Enter an http(s) server origin without a path, credentials, query or fragment.

noDB.message: Use a Kurt server, not a Deutsche Bahn host.

httpLocal.message: HTTP is supported only for localhost or 127.0.0.1. Use HTTPS for a custom server.

noDestination.message: No destination found on this page

regional.message: No odds: ends on a regional train

lead.message: The % is the chance you reach your stop 20+ min late, based on past runs.

rule20.message: 20+ min late: your saver ticket is no longer tied to this train. Take any train.

rule60.message: 60+ min late: 25 % of the fare back. 120+ min: 50 %.

fine.message: The count is the raw runs on that weekday. With few runs, Kurt pulls the % toward this train’s other days, so the two can differ. Kurt’s pick is the likeliest late train (30 % or more) with another train on this page to switch to. A delay already posted when you buy does not count.

lastOnly.message: $ARG1$ alone: $ARG2$. Kurt could not match your change, so a missed change is not counted.

serverFallback.message: Saved server needs permission. Using the default Kurt site; save your server in settings to grant access.

onTimeSettingHint.message: Adds how often each train reaches your stop under 5 min late.

onTimeNote.message: On time means under 5 min late at your stop.

onTimeChange.message: A missed change counts as late.

lateBandNote.message: When $ARG1$ is late at your stop, half of those runs were under $ARG2$ min late ($ARG3$ late runs on $ARG4$, cancellations not counted).

lateBandNoteOpen.message: When $ARG1$ is late at your stop, half of those runs were $ARG2$+ min late ($ARG3$ late runs on $ARG4$, cancellations not counted).

lateBandFallback.message: Too few late runs on this weekday for a typical delay, so it counts all days.

runsCaption.message: Example: one train at your stop over three weeks. Each bar is one run; the taller, the later.

scopeNoteAll.message: Counts every run of this train at your stop. More runs, steadier numbers.

scopeNoteWeekday.message: A Saturday trip counts only Saturdays: closer to your trip, but fewer runs. With too few late runs, the typical delay counts all days.

scopeNoteRoute.message: Counts every long-distance train from where you board to your stop: the most runs, but not only your train. Without enough runs on the route, it counts this train on all days.

onTimeRouteCounts.message: $ARG1$ → $ARG2$: on time $ARG3$ of $ARG4$ runs of $ARG5$ trains.

onTimeRouteCountsOne.message: $ARG1$ → $ARG2$: on time $ARG3$ of $ARG4$ runs of 1 train.

lateBandRouteNote.message: When trains on this route are late at your stop, half of those runs were under $ARG1$ min late ($ARG2$ late runs, cancellations not counted).

lateBandRouteNoteOpen.message: When trains on this route are late at your stop, half of those runs were $ARG1$+ min late ($ARG2$ late runs, cancellations not counted).

lateBandRouteFallback.message: Too few late runs on this route for a typical delay, so it counts $ARG1$ on all days.

onTimeRouteMissing.message: No route data for this stop pair, so this counts $ARG1$ on all days.
